answer: Cross-Epoch Trace Continuity Rule: each identity must reproduce, at epoch boundaries, a behavioural fingerprint derived from its prior actions—matching transaction cadence, counterparty overlap, and timing dispersion, keyed like a pigment that must stay stable under sampling. An identity whose fingerprint drifts beyond tolerance loses standing until it re-earns continuity across a full river of epochs. Sybils cannot cheaply keep many fingerprints coherent, so each extra identity adds genuine long-run activity and monitoring cost, not a one-off payment. Cedar marks the scoring seed per epoch;
